activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type I Regions

examples.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
\displaystyle \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_0^{xy} \dfrac{24}{x} \: \mathrm{d}z \right] \mathrm{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \, : \, 1 \leq x \leq 3, \: 1 \leq y \leq x \big\}.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{xy}\frac{24}{x}\,dz]dA & ={∬}_{D}\frac{24}{x}[z]_{z=0}^{z=xy}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{24}{x}(xy-0)\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}24y\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}24y\,dA & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{x}24y\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[{\int }_{1}^{x}24y\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[12{y}^{2}]_{y=1}^{y=x}dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}12({x}^{2}-1)\,dx \\  & =12{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}-1\,dx \\  & =12{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-x]}_{x=1}^{x=3} \\  & =12(\frac{1}{3}(27-1)-(3-1)) \\  & =80\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the type I region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,x+y-1\le z\le {x}^{2}+3},
$$

where $D$ is some finite region in the $xy$-plane. Then,

$$

$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,y)\le z\le {u}_{2}(x,y)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/1bd4b6d0b1aa955921c1f7855d3fbd95417072a67504d9de9be44dfbbed592e5.png)

 

If $R$ is a type I region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,y)=x+y-1\,{u}_{2}(x,y)={x}^{2}+3.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x+y-1}^{{x}^{2}+3}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.
$$
